stem: A written information security policy approved by the board is best described as which control category?

options.why: Policies, risk assessments and security planning are managerial controls: they direct how security is governed.
Directive is a control type, describing what the control does. The question asked for the category. A policy is managerial in category and directive in type.
Operational controls are executed by people day to day, such as awareness training or guard patrols. Writing and approving the policy itself is managerial.
Technical controls are implemented in hardware or software. A document is not.

stem: A nightly backup job is best classified as which control category and type?

options.why: It is implemented in software, and it acts after an incident to restore what was lost.
The category is right and the type is wrong. A backup prevents nothing; it repairs afterwards.
The type is right and the category is wrong. An automated job is technical, not a human process.
Both are wrong. It is not governance, and it does not stand in for a control you could not implement.

stem: A sign at the car park entrance reads 'Warning: this area is under video surveillance.' The sign itself is which control type?

options.why: It discourages an attacker by changing their decision. It physically blocks nothing.
An attacker who ignores the sign is not stopped by it. Nothing is prevented.
The cameras are detective. The sign announcing them is deterrent.
A compensating control substitutes for a control you cannot implement. The sign is not standing in for anything.

stem: Which physical control is preventive rather than deterrent?

options.why: A vehicle physically cannot pass them. The attacker's intent is irrelevant.

options.text: Security lighting in the car park
options.why: Lighting makes an attacker feel exposed, which discourages. It stops nobody who proceeds anyway.

options.text: A visible camera dome in the lobby
options.why: Visible cameras deter, and they detect. They do not prevent entry.

options.text: A sign warning that trespassers will be prosecuted
options.why: Warning signs are the textbook deterrent.

stem: A legacy manufacturing system cannot be patched because the vendor no longer exists and the software will not run on a supported OS. The organisation places it on an isolated VLAN with strict ACLs and enhanced monitoring. What kind of control is this?

options.why: The control you wanted, patching, is impossible, so another control is put in place to meet the objective by different means. It is documented as an exception in the risk register.
Corrective controls repair after an incident. Nothing has happened here; this is chosen in advance.
The monitoring component is detective, but the isolation and ACLs are the substance, and the reason for the whole arrangement is substitution.
Directive controls instruct people what to do. This is a technical arrangement.

stem: Which scenario describes a corrective control rather than a compensating one?

options.text: Restoring a database from backup after a failed update corrupted it
options.why: The incident happened and the control repairs the damage. That is corrective.

options.text: Requiring two approvers because the application cannot enforce separation of duties
options.why: The desired control is unavailable, so a different one substitutes for it in advance. That is compensating.

options.text: Adding MFA to a system whose password policy cannot be strengthened
options.why: Again a substitute for a control that cannot be implemented, chosen before anything goes wrong.

options.text: Isolating an unpatchable device on its own network segment
options.why: The classic compensating control for a device that cannot be patched.

stem: Which TWO controls are preventive rather than deterrent? (Choose two.)

options.why: A vehicle physically cannot pass. The attacker's intent is irrelevant, which is what makes it preventive.
It physically stops a second person following the first through the door.

options.text: A sign reading 'These premises are under video surveillance'
options.why: A sign persuades. Anyone who ignores it walks straight past, so it deters and prevents nothing.

options.text: Security lighting across the car park
options.why: Lighting makes an attacker feel exposed. It blocks nobody.
A policy is directive in type and managerial in category. It instructs, it does not prevent.

stem: A SIEM rule raises an alert when the same user authenticates from two countries within an hour. Which control type is the rule?

options.text: Detective: it identifies the event after it has happened and raises it for action
options.why: An alert is the signature output of a detective control. Both logins already succeeded; the rule found out.

options.text: Preventive: the alert stops the second login
options.why: An alert stops nothing. Had the system refused the second login, that refusal would be preventive; raising it afterwards is detective.

options.text: Corrective: it returns the account to a safe state
options.why: Nothing was repaired. Disabling the account or forcing a reset after the alert would be corrective; the rule itself only reports.

options.text: Technical: it is implemented in software
options.why: Technical is the category, and it is correct on that axis. The question asked for the type, which is what the control does about the event.

stem: A badge reader refuses entry to anyone without a valid card, and a camera system records the lobby. Which control types are these, in that order?

options.why: The reader physically stops entry. The recording stops nobody; it gives you evidence afterwards.
The reader does not merely discourage; a determined person without a card is still stopped, which makes it preventive.
A recording prevents nothing. It is reviewed after the event, which is the definition of detective.
Those are categories. The question asks for types.

stem: An organisation updates its acceptable use policy to state that personal cloud storage must not be used for company files, and every employee signs the new version. Which control type is the policy?

options.text: Directive: it instructs staff on the behaviour expected of them
options.why: A policy tells people who intend to comply what to do. That is a directive control, whatever topic it covers.

options.text: Deterrent: it discourages employees from using personal storage
options.why: A deterrent is aimed at someone who intends to do harm and warns them off. The policy is aimed at the compliant and tells them the rule.

options.text: Preventive: with the policy in force, files cannot reach personal storage
options.why: A policy prevents nothing by itself. A DLP rule that blocks the upload would be the preventive control enforcing it.

options.text: Managerial: it is a document approved by management
options.why: Managerial is the right category. The question asked for the type.

stem: Which control is operational rather than managerial or technical?

options.text: Security guards performing hourly patrols of the data centre
options.why: People performing a process on a schedule is the operational category.

options.text: The annual risk assessment approved by the chief information security officer
options.why: A risk assessment is a governing decision document. That is managerial.

options.text: The access control policy requiring multifactor authentication for administrators
options.why: A policy is managerial. It governs; it does not carry anything out.

options.text: The multifactor authentication system enforcing the second factor
options.why: A system enforcing with no person in the loop is technical.

stem: A payment application is required to log every administrative action, but the vendor's software cannot write audit logs. The team places a network tap and records every administrative session to the application instead. Which control type is the session recording?

options.text: Compensating: it stands in for the audit logging the application cannot provide
options.why: The stem says the required control could not be implemented and this one was put in its place. That makes it compensating, whatever its own mechanism.

options.text: Detective: a recording identifies what happened after the fact
options.why: By mechanism it does detect, but a substitute for a required control is classified as compensating. The stem spelled out the substitution.

options.text: Corrective: it fixes the application's missing capability
options.why: Nothing was repaired and no incident happened. A control chosen in advance because the wanted one is impossible is compensating.

options.text: Physical: a tap is a piece of hardware
options.why: That is a category argument, and a weak one; the question asks for the type.

stem: Which TWO are detective controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: An analyst reviewing firewall logs every morning
options.why: Reviewing logs finds out what happened. It stops nothing and fixes nothing, which is exactly detective.

options.text: An intrusion detection system on a network tap
options.why: An IDS watches a copy of the traffic and raises an alert. Detection is in the name.

options.text: A warning sign at the perimeter fence
options.why: A sign notices nothing. It discourages, which is deterrent.
Encryption prevents disclosure. It reports nothing, so it cannot be detective.

stem: Which control is deterrent rather than directive?

options.text: A sign stating that the premises are patrolled by guard dogs
options.why: It is aimed at someone considering an intrusion and warns them off. That is a deterrent.

options.text: A sign instructing visitors to sign in at reception
options.why: That sign gives an instruction to people who intend to comply. It is directive.
Training tells people how to behave. Directive.
A policy instructs. It threatens nobody, so it is directive, not deterrent.

stem: A company documents a procedure for provisioning new starters, and the help desk follows it every Monday morning. Which categories do the written procedure and the weekly execution belong to?

options.why: The document governs how the work is done, which is managerial. People carrying it out is operational.
The procedure document carries nothing out. A written control that governs is managerial; only its execution is operational.
A procedure is not a system enforcing anything. Technical controls act without a person in the loop.
The help desk performing the steps is people doing a process. That is operational, not a management decision.

stem: Which of these controls is directive?

options.text: A notice warning that trespassers will be prosecuted
options.why: It announces a consequence to people who intend not to comply. That is deterrent.
Lighting discourages an intruder by making them feel exposed. Deterrent, not directive.

options.text: A procedure telling staff to escort visitors at all times
options.why: It instructs people who intend to comply on what to do. That is a directive control.

options.text: A turnstile that admits one badge holder at a time
options.why: It physically stops anyone without a badge, whatever their intent. Preventive.

stem: The risk committee decides and documents an annual review of every critical vendor. Separately, a security analyst reads the firewall logs each morning and escalates anything unusual. Which categories do these controls belong to?

options.why: The committee decides and governs; it does not perform a routine process. Its review programme is managerial.

options.text: Managerial, then technical, because the logs come from a firewall
options.why: The firewall is technical. The analyst reading its logs is a person performing a process, which is operational.
The two are the wrong way round: the committee's documented programme is managerial and the analyst's daily work is operational.

options.text: The vendor review is managerial; the daily log review is operational
options.why: A governing decision and its document is managerial. A person carrying out a process is operational, even when the material they read comes from a system.

stem: A data center replaces its single lobby door with an access control vestibule, where the inner door opens only after the outer door has closed and the visitor is verified. How is this control best classified?

options.why: Doors and the space between them are physical barriers, not software or a system making a decision. The type is right but the category is not.
A vestibule blocks entry. A detective control would record or alert and let the person through.
The vestibule is made of doors and space, so it is physical, and it stops an unverified person from walking in, so it is preventive.
The control is a structure, not a procedure people carry out, and it physically holds people back, which is more than discouraging them.

stem: A laminated card beside the firewall console lists the steps an engineer must follow before opening any inbound port. Engineers are expected to follow it and nothing enforces it. Which control type is the card?

options.why: It tells willing people what to do. Nothing stops or punishes someone who ignores it, which is what makes it directive.
A deterrent is aimed at people who might break the rules and gives them a reason not to. The card is guidance for people who intend to comply.
A preventive control blocks an action whether or not the person cooperates. A card cannot stop an engineer who skips it.
Operational is a control category, which describes who carries the control out. The question asks for the type, which is when and how it acts.

stem: A legacy appliance cannot support multi-factor authentication, but the security standard requires it for administrator logins. Which action is a compensating control?

options.text: Sign an exception memo that accepts the risk until the appliance is eventually replaced
options.why: A signed exception documents that the risk is accepted. It adds no protection, so it is risk acceptance and not a compensating control.

options.text: Route administrator access through a hardened jump host with per-session approval and recording
options.why: It substitutes for the missing control with other protection aimed at the same risk: who can reach the appliance and what they do.

options.text: Email every administrator a reminder to choose strong passwords for their accounts
options.why: A reminder is guidance for people who intend to comply. It does not give the appliance any protection in place of MFA.

options.text: Show a login banner warning that all administrator activity may be reviewed later
options.why: A banner may discourage misuse, but it does not stop a stolen password from being used, so it does not stand in for MFA.

stem: An endpoint agent spots ransomware behavior on a laptop, kills the process, isolates the host and restores the files it encrypted from local shadow copies. Which control type best describes the response action?

options.why: The alert that started this was detective. The question is about the response, which acts to reverse the harm and not just to report it.
Preventive controls stop an action before it happens. Here the encryption had already begun and the control undid it.
A compensating control stands in for one that cannot be used. Nothing here replaces a missing control, it cleans up after an event.
The action repairs damage after the event has started. Detection triggered it, but what the control does is reverse and contain the harm.

stem: Every administrator login to the billing system shows the message: authorized users only, activity is logged, misuse will be reported to law enforcement. Which control type is the message?

options.why: A directive tells people who intend to comply how to behave. This message is meant to make someone who might misuse access reconsider.
It is aimed at someone considering misuse and gives them a reason to think again, without blocking anything.
A preventive control would stop the login or the action. The message lets anyone with credentials continue.
Logging is detective, but the message itself only warns about the logging. It is the warning that is being classified.

stem: The security team runs a simulated phishing campaign each quarter and sends follow-up coaching to employees who click. Which description fits the activity?

options.text: Managerial category, because it is part of the security program
options.why: Managerial controls are decisions, policies and planning. Running the campaign is the activity that those decisions lead to.

options.text: Technical category, because it uses email software
options.why: Technical controls are carried out by a system acting on its own. Here people design the campaign and respond to the results.

options.text: Detective type, which is the same thing as a category
options.why: Detective is a type. Category and type are separate questions, and the activity is described by its category here.

options.text: Operational category, because people carry it out day to day
options.why: Operational controls are performed by people as an ongoing practice. Running the campaign and coaching is that kind of work.

stem: Company laptops have full-disk encryption enabled so that a lost device does not expose its data. Which category and type does this control belong to?

options.why: A system enforces it, so it is technical, and it stops the data from being read by whoever finds the device, so it is preventive.
Corrective controls repair harm after an event. Encryption works before any loss occurs.
Operational controls depend on people doing something each time. Encryption runs without anyone acting, so it is technical.
A policy requiring encryption would be managerial and directive. The encryption itself is the technical measure.

stem: Which TWO activities are corrective controls? (Choose two.)

options.text: Reviewing authentication logs each Friday for unusual sign-ins
options.why: Reviewing logs finds problems and reports them. It is detective, not corrective.

options.text: Restoring a corrupted customer database from the last good backup
options.why: This repairs damage after it has happened, which is what a corrective control does.

options.text: Requiring a badge to enter the server room
options.why: The badge reader stops entry beforehand, so it is preventive.

options.text: Reimaging an infected laptop from a known clean image
options.why: This returns the system to a known good state after a compromise, which is corrective.

options.text: Having every employee sign the acceptable use policy
options.why: A signed policy tells people what is expected. It is directive and repairs nothing.

stem: Which THREE items are physical controls? (Choose three.)

options.text: Bollards in front of the building entrance
options.why: They are solid objects that stop vehicles, so they are physical.
A policy is a managerial control. It sets the rules but is not itself a barrier.

options.text: A locked cage around the network equipment
options.why: A lock and a cage are physical barriers around the equipment, which makes them physical controls.
An intrusion detection system is a technical control. It works on traffic, not on the building.

options.text: Motion-activated lighting around the loading dock
options.why: Lighting is a physical measure that discourages and exposes intruders.

stem: A network sensor that only copies traffic from a mirror port and raises alerts is moved in line with the traffic and set to drop packets that match attack signatures. How does its control type change?

options.text: It stays detective, because the product is still called a sensor
options.why: Type depends on how the control acts, not on its name. Dropping packets blocks the action.

options.text: It changes from preventive to corrective, because it acts on live traffic
options.why: Before the move it only alerted, so it was not preventive. Corrective controls repair harm after the event.

options.text: It changes from detective to preventive, because it now blocks traffic
options.why: The type follows what the control does. Alerting is detective, and dropping the traffic before it arrives is preventive.

options.text: It changes from technical to physical, because it is now inline
options.why: Position in the network does not change the category. It is a system acting on traffic, so it stays technical.

stem: Each Monday an auditor reviews last week's privileged account activity against approved change tickets and flags anything unexplained. Which category and type describe this review?

options.why: The type is right, but a person is doing the review, which makes it operational and not technical.
People perform it regularly, so it is operational, and it finds problems after the fact without blocking them, so it is detective.
A review after the week is over cannot stop the activity it examines, so it is not preventive.
A directive control tells people what to do. This review checks what they did.

stem: A facilities manager mounts decoy camera housings on the loading dock because real cameras are not yet funded. Which control type do the decoys provide?

options.why: They make a would-be intruder think the area is watched, but they record nothing and block nothing.
A detective control records or alerts. A decoy does neither, so no event is ever noticed.
A preventive control stops an intruder who ignores it. A determined person can walk past a decoy.
Corrective controls restore things after an incident. A decoy does nothing once something has happened.

stem: A policy bans USB storage devices, but staff keep plugging them in. The security manager wants a control that does not rely on people choosing to comply. What should be added?

options.text: A new reminder poster about the USB policy in the break room
options.why: A poster is directive guidance. It is aimed at people who already intend to comply.

options.text: A monthly report listing the removable devices that were connected
options.why: A report is detective. It finds out afterward and does not stop the device being used.

options.text: A second signed acknowledgment of the USB policy from each employee
options.why: A signature adds accountability but not a barrier, so people who ignore the policy can still plug in the drive.

options.text: An endpoint setting that blocks USB mass storage on all laptops
options.why: A technical control acts whether or not the person cooperates, which makes it preventive.

stem: The badge reader on the server room door fails and the vendor needs a week to repair it. Until then a guard checks each person's identity against an access list and signs them in. Which control type is the guard's check?

options.why: Corrective controls repair the effects of an event. The guard does not fix the reader, they stand in for it while it is broken.
It temporarily takes the place of the failed reader and aims at the same protection, which is why it is compensating.
A visible guard may discourage some people, but the guard is there to check identities and keep unauthorized people out.
Signing people in leaves a record, but the check happens before entry and decides who goes through.
